snippet.title: Trump’s Inner Circle & Use of Military Power | The War Cabinet (full documentary) | FRONTLINE (PBS)
snippet.description:
A 90-minute documentary examining the key players behind President Trump’s expansive use of the U.S. military during his second term. 

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

When Donald Trump campaigned for his second term, he made a repeated promise: no new wars.

Drawing on in-depth interviews with President Trump’s allies and associates, officials from his first administration, and his critics, as well as former diplomats, military experts and journalists, “The War Cabinet” traces how, after vowing to end wars, not start them, Trump assembled a team of loyalists, and together they pursued a much different course. 

That team includes Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, longtime aide Stephen Miller, Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, Vice President JD Vance and outgoing Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard. The documentary tells the story of how the cabinet, a group whose members had diverse life stories and worldviews, came together to support the president in his quest to demonstrate the United States’ military might on the international stage.

The film traces how Trump has increasingly sought to cement his legacy and achieve U.S. policy objectives through military strength; how the administration has engaged militarily everywhere from Yemen, to the waters off Venezuela, to Iran; and the roles of key players in Trump’s second-term military decisions. With the Iran conflict now in its third month and threatening to define Trump’s second term, “The War Cabinet” is a must-watch documentary on how the president who promised peace has become a wartime president — and the ongoing ramifications.

The producers are Michael Kirk, Mike Wiser, Vanessa Fica, Elliott Choi and Philip Bennett. The reporters are Vanessa Fica and Brooke Nelson Alexander. The managing editor of FRONTLINE is Andrew Metz. snippet.title: Mount St. Helens: Deadly Eruption | America's Most Catastrophic Volcanic Disaster
snippet.description:
Experience the raw, devastating power of nature with "Deadly Eruption: Mt. St. Helens." This gripping documentary, directed by Lenny Newman, meticulously reconstructs the catastrophic 1980 eruption of Mount St. Helens, revealing the immense geological forces at play and the profound impact on the landscape and those caught in its path.

Deadly Eruption: Mt. St. Helens (2025)

Director: Lenny Newman
Writers: Lenny Newman
Stars: Gregory Walters (Narrator),
Genre: Documentary, Disaster, Science, History, Nature, Geology
Country: United Kingdom
Language: English
Also Known As: Mount St Helen
Release Date: January 6, 2025
Filming Location: Mount St. Helens, Washington State, USA (historical footage)

Synopsis:

In the heart of the Pacific Northwest, a sleeping giant awakened on May 18, 1980. Directed by Lenny Newman, "Deadly Eruption: Mt. St. Helens" chronicles the catastrophic eruption of this iconic volcano, a pivotal event in geological history.

The film begins by exploring the subtle warnings that preceded the explosion, culminating in one of the most violent volcanic events ever recorded—a massive landslide, an earth-shattering explosion, and eruptions that continued for six years. Through vivid accounts and compelling visuals, the documentary portrays the decimation of forests, the transformation of rivers, and the tragic loss of lives, serving as a stark reminder of Earth's immense, untamed power.

snippet.title: Pablo Escobar’s Rise & Fall | The Godfather of Cocaine (full documentary) | FRONTLINE (PBS)
snippet.description:
An investigation into the bloody rise and fall of Pablo Escobar and how the empire he built set the stage for the modern narco-trafficking industry. (Aired 1995)

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

This archival FRONTLINE documentary examines how one drug, cocaine, began flowing into the U.S. at an industrial scale in the 1970s and 1980s — and the pivotal role of the notorious Colombian drug lord Pablo Escobar, the boss of the Medellin cocaine cartel. 

With remarkable access to Escobar’s family, relatives of his victims, and both Colombian and U.S. officials, “The Godfather of Cocaine” traces how Escobar built a multi-billion-dollar fortune through international cocaine smuggling alliances and a sophisticated operation to traffic cocaine into the U.S.

Escobar maintained his dominance through violent repression and extreme brutality, with his cartel funneling drug profits into attacks and killings that brought Colombia to a state of virtual civil war. 

Colombian police and the U.S. DEA hunted Escobar down and assassinated him in 1993, but it didn’t end the narco-trafficking model he built. 

“The death of Escobar was a landmark in the history of an industry, but it wasn't a victory, in the sense that it didn’t put anything out of business,” Senate investigator Jack Blum said in the documentary. “It didn't change the pace of trafficking. It didn't raise or lower the price of cocaine.”

“The Godfather of Cocaine” was produced by William Cran and Stephanie Tepper. The associate producers were Christopher Buchanan and Marcela Gaviria. The documentary was written and directed by William Cran. Cran, a prolific and acclaimed documentary filmmaker, passed away in 2025: https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/frontline/article/remembering-william-cran-prolific-and-acclaimed-documentary-filmmaker/

snippet.description:
19S - A visual testimony of the 2017 Mexico earthquake, where tragedy revealed the power of collective action and human resilience.

Director: Luis Arango
Writers: Luis Arango
Genre: Documentary, Social, History
Country: Mexico
Language: Spanish
Release Date: 2017
Filming Location: Mexico

Synopsis:
The Day Mexico Stood Together is a powerful audiovisual project that documents the aftermath of the September 19, 2017 earthquake in Mexico—a tragedy that claimed hundreds of lives and affected thousands.

Through a unique combination of documentary storytelling and citizen photography, the film captures raw, unfiltered moments of solidarity, chaos, and reconstruction. Built from an extensive archive curated by photographer Luis Arango and the magazine Cuartoscuro, the project brings together images taken not only by professionals but also by ordinary people who lived through the disaster.

More than a recount of events, the documentary becomes a collective memory—revealing how society reacts under extreme conditions, how communities self-organize, and how human connection emerges in times of crisis. It is both a historical record and a reflection on resilience, unity, and the social fabric of a nation under pressure.

snippet.description:
Foucault Against Himself – A profound exploration of the life, ideas, and inner contradictions of one of the most influential thinkers of the 20th century.

Director: François Caillat
Writers: François Caillat, Jean-Paul Fargier
Stars: Michel Foucault (archival footage), Philippe Artières, Leo Bersani, Georges Didi-Huberman, Paul Veyne
Genre: Documentary, Biography, Philosophy, History
Country: France
Language: French
Also Known As: Foucault contre lui-même
Release Date: 2014
Filming Location: France

Synopsis:
Foucault Against Himself (original title: Foucault contre lui-même) examines the intellectual and personal evolution of French philosopher Michel Foucault. Through archival footage, interviews, and commentary from scholars and close acquaintances, the film traces Foucault’s journey from the early works on madness and punishment to his later reflections on sexuality, power, and truth. Director François Caillat constructs a nuanced portrait of a man perpetually questioning his own ideas — a thinker “against himself.” The documentary captures the intensity, contradictions, and humanity behind Foucault’s revolutionary thought, offering insight into his lifelong struggle to understand freedom and the self.

snippet.title: Examining U.S.-Saudi Ties | The Crown Prince & the President (full documentary) | FRONTLINE (PBS)
snippet.description:
Martin Smith examines the alliance between Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and President Donald Trump in this 90-minute documentary. 

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

What is behind the alliance between President Donald Trump and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS), and what are the ramifications for the U.S., Saudi Arabia and the Middle East as a whole? 

Answers unfold in “The Crown Prince & the President,” the latest documentary from an award-winning team that includes directors, writers and producers Martin Smith and Marcela Gaviria, and co-producers Scott Anger and Jennifer Brooks. 
 
“‘The Crown Prince & the President’ is based on over 100 interviews I have done in the U.S. and abroad,” says Smith, who also serves as correspondent and has covered the U.S.-Saudi relationship for more than 20 years. “Our investigation is an incisive look at the forces binding the two men and their countries together, and what each stands to gain — from ambitions for a new Middle East, to arms deals, investments and personal profit.”
 
Over the course of the documentary, that story is told with insights from former U.S. officials and diplomats, members of the Saudi government, Trump administration insiders, Saudi dissidents, human rights and foreign policy experts, and journalists who have covered financial ties between the Trump family and Saudi Arabia. 
 
What emerges is a sharp chronicle of how the alliance between the crown prince who promised reform and the Trump administration has grown, despite MBS’ crackdown on dissent and the murder of journalist Jamal Khashoggi, in which MBS denied involvement.
 
The documentary also offers a powerful examination of the Trump administration’s foreign policy strategy for Saudi Arabia, and the implications for the surrounding region, the U.S. and the world.

snippet.title: For-Profit Adoptions & Misconduct Allegations (full documentary) | FRONTLINE (PBS) + Retro Report
snippet.description:
With Retro Report, an investigation into how so-called “baby brokers” have targeted pregnant women and families looking to adopt, and an epicenter of the problem in Utah.

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

The adoption industry in the U.S. is a multi-billion-dollar business, where demand outpaces the number of infants available for adoption. In “Baby Brokers,” FRONTLINE and Retro Report investigate a loosely-regulated corner of the industry described as “adoption tourism” and examine how allegations of misconduct involving for-profit agencies and brokers have mounted. 

The documentary illuminates a patchwork system, where allegations of misconduct have stacked up in states like Utah with historically more permissive laws. 

In the documentary, the head of an adoption agency in Utah says that out-of-state adoptions fulfill an important need. But other sources express concern about how brokers and agencies have used cash and housing offers as incentives for vulnerable women in other states.

In recent months, Utah has moved to tighten some of its laws in response to mounting criticisms from birth mothers, their advocates, and adoptive parents. And at the federal level, lawmakers from a number of states are backing a bipartisan bill aimed at reining in unlicensed brokers who funnel pregnant women and families across state lines for adoptions.

As the debate over “adoption tourism” continues, “Baby Brokers” is a must-watch exploration of the practice, the role of brokers, and the impact on both birth mothers and adoptive parents.
